related_questions.question: When does a UTI become an emergency?

text_blocks.snippet: A urinary tract infection (UTI) can become an emergency if it progresses to involve the kidneys (pyelonephritis) or leads to urosepsis. Symptoms like high fever, severe back or side pain, vomiting, and confusion, especially in older adults, warrant immediate medical attention at an emergency room. Prompt treatment is crucial to prevent serious complications like kidney damage or sepsis.
snippet_highlighted_words: if it progresses to involve the kidneys (pyelonephritis) or leads to urosepsis

text_blocks.snippet: When a UTI becomes an emergency:

list.title: Kidney infection (pyelonephritis):
list.snippet: If a UTI spreads to the kidneys, it can cause severe symptoms like high fever, chills, back or side pain, nausea, and vomiting. This is a serious condition that requires immediate medical care, often in an emergency room.

list.title: Urosepsis:
list.snippet: In rare cases, bacteria from a UTI can enter the bloodstream and cause sepsis, a life-threatening condition that requires intensive care. Symptoms of urosepsis include fever, confusion, rapid breathing, and a drop in blood pressure.

list.title: Sepsis:
list.snippet: A UTI can progress to sepsis if bacteria from the urinary tract enter the bloodstream and cause a systemic inflammatory response. Sepsis is a medical emergency that can be life-threatening and requires immediate medical attention.

text_blocks.snippet: Symptoms that indicate a UTI is worsening and may require emergency care:

list.snippet: Symptoms that don't improve with treatment

text_blocks.snippet: When to seek immediate medical attention:

list.snippet: If you experience any of the symptoms listed above, seek immediate medical attention at an emergency room.
If you are pregnant, have diabetes, or have other underlying health conditions, seek medical attention promptly at the first sign of a UTI.
If you have a catheter, you are also at higher risk and should seek medical attention for any UTI symptoms.
If you have recurrent UTIs, seek medical advice to identify potential underlying causes.
If you are unsure whether your symptoms warrant emergency care, it is always best to err on the side of caution and seek medical advice.
